A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIM datasets and DIM-4.6B framework. Text, tables, figures, and other material support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes readable Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIM model evaluations on generation and editing benchmarks, data-composition and CoT-component ablations, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds MagicBrush evaluation, designer and initialization experiments, annotation-quality assessments involving human raters, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The core architecture, four-step blueprints, and staged training procedure remain. v3 adds lightweight fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-VL-3B on DIM-Edit blueprints and describes internal self-play inference (Section 4.3, Table 7). The frozen Q3B row reproduces v1's externally labeled Q3B results, so that relabeling alone does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Original training corpora and benchmarks remain. v3 adds MagicBrush test evaluation against human-edited targets and substantially broadens demonstrated task requirements through knowledge-dependent, temporal, geometric, and reference-free editing scenarios (Appendix B), including implicit prime-number counting, rusting nails, and map-to-photo generation.

E2.justification: The original generation, ImgEdit, and GEdit comparator sets are retained after relocation. The new MagicBrush comparison evaluates FluxEdit, FLUX.1 Fill, RF-Solver Edit, ACE++, and ICEdit alongside previously compared methods (v3 Table 5), substantially expanding the editing approaches compared.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets, learning rates, batch sizes, GenEval prompt rewriting, and GPT-4.1 benchmark judging remain unchanged. New protocols include MagicBrush L1/CLIP-I/DINO evaluation, raw-prompt and initialization controls, timing over 100 samples at 1024×1024 with 30 generation steps, and quality assessments using 30K GPT-4.1-rated pairs plus 100 samples assessed by three humans.

E4.justification: v3 preserves the original data-composition and CoT-component ablations while adding designer-free inference, additional designers, internal-designer fine-tuning, and initialization comparisons. Appendix A tests identical CoT blueprints on Janus-4o and Step1X-Edit; Appendices B and D add extensive mechanism-oriented examples, six failure cases, and automated/human annotation-quality analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated model runs, random-seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3 adds sample and annotator counts and aggregate quality percentages, but these describe new evaluations rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained headline results remain 0.77 GenEval, 5.50 MJHQ-30K FID, 3.67 ImgEdit, and 6.18 GEdit full-set overall. New results include MagicBrush L1/CLIP-I/DINO of 0.065/0.928/0.882, a 3.61 ImgEdit score for the fine-tuned internal designer, and human-assessment rates of 89% optimized-instruction preference and 81% perfect EII alignment. These are additional evaluations and variants, not improvements to unchanged-setting headline scores.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. v3's newly stated flow-matching objective and expanded curriculum-learning and CoT explanations do not introduce new formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution summary revise the claimed competitor-size advantage from 10× to 5× and focus that outperformance statement on ImgEdit. The central role-rebalancing argument, dataset contributions, and abstract/conclusion claims of state-of-the-art or competitive editing performance remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of designer adaptation, initialization, and differing responses to CoT inputs. It substantially expands applicability boundaries through failures involving extensive object manipulation, text, geometry, and transformations that break source-image alignment. Appendix B links text-rendering limitations to 32× VAE compression and discusses the efficiency–fidelity tradeoff; Appendix D interprets annotation errors.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the flow-matching objective, UltraEdit filtering thresholds (CLIP and DINOv2 above 0.9; SSIM above 0.8), exclusion of rainbow prompts, and detailed annotation prompts for all 21 DIM-T2I dimensions. These clarify existing construction procedures rather than establish changed datasets. The abstract also changes the reported dataset/model release status from planned to available.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens the literature grounding for its annotation dimensions through understanding, OCR, mathematics, science, and instruction-following benchmarks in Appendix E. It also introduces references supporting new editing comparisons and designers and supplies citations for previously named baselines. Section 2's original connector-versus-integrative positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title and author wording change, DIM-T2I motivation expands, and several passages and captions are tightened. Ablations gain named subtopics, while GEdit details and annotation dimensions move into organized appendices. Most original section ordering and prose remain; much of the expansion consists of additional scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is extensively redrawn and relocated, Figure 2 replaces an illustrative example, and Figure 3 reorganizes the retained images with color-coded columns. GEdit tables move or split between the main text and appendix. Numerous new comparison, failure, and quality-assessment displays are added, and the original dimension list expands into Figures 19–20.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central blueprint and data-quality argument through designer controls, initialization experiments, same-blueprint baseline comparisons, and automated/human annotation audits. Filtering details and annotation prompts improve reproducibility, while concrete failure cases clarify applicability beyond v1's limited discussion. These address important gaps despite unchanged headline scores. Some designer fine-tuning and timing details remain unspecified, and uncertainty reporting is still absent, but the overall evidential and transparency gains are substantial.
